13. EMERGENCY CONTRACEPTION

•Indication: Women who do not wish to conceive should be offered EC after UPSI that has taken place on any day of a natural menstrual cycle.
•After pregnancy: Women who do not wish to conceive should be offered EC after:
✓UPSI from Day 21 after childbirth
✓UPSI from Day 5 after abortion, miscarriage, ectopic pregnancy or uterine evacuation for gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD).
•Hormonal contraception incorrectly: Women who do not wish to conceive should be offered EC after UPSI if their regular contraception has been compromised or has been used incorrectly

 

There are 3 methods of EC:

1.CU – IUD
2.UPA – EC
3.LNG – ECG

 

Mode of action:

•Sperm are viable in the female genital tract for about 5 days after UPSI. If ovulation occurs within those 5 days, fertilization could take place and a woman is at risk of pregnancy.
1.Cu-lUD: Inhibition of fertilization by its toxic effect on sperm and ova. Copper has been shown to adversely affect the motility and viability of sperm and the viability and transport of ova. It is the most effective method of EC
2.UPA: UPA 30 mg – a selective progesterone receptor modulator – acts by delaying ovulation for at least 5 days, until sperm from the UPSI for which EC was taken are no longer viable.
3.LNG: LNG-EC inhibits ovulation, delaying or preventing follicular rupture and causing luteal dysfunction.

Oral EC

•EC providers should advise women that UPA-EC has been demonstrated to be effective for EC up to 120 hours of UPSI
•LNG-EC is licensed for EC up to 72 hours after UPSI. The evidence suggests that LNG-EC is ineffective if taken more than 96 hours after UPSI.
•UPA-EC has been demonstrated to be more effective than LNG-EC.
•Oral EC administered after ovulation is ineffective

Effect of Weight/BMI:

•Cu-IUD: Effectiveness of the Cu-IUD is not known to be affected by weight or BMI.

Oral EC: It is possible that higher weight or BMI could reduce the effectiveness of oral EC, particularly LNG-EC.

Consideration before offering EC:

1.Hours passed from UPSI
2.Date of M/C
3.R/O Contraindications of EC
4.If LNG, double check indications of Double Dose (3 mg vs 1.5 mg)

Double dose of LNG – EC is given in:

1.Wt >70 kg
2.BMI >26
3.Taking enzyme inducing drugs

Inducers of hepatic CYP450 enzymes:

•EC providers should advise women using enzyme-inducing drugs that the effectiveness of UPA-EC and LNG-EC could be reduced.
•Women requiring EC who are using enzyme-inducing drugs should be offered a Cu-IUD if appropriate.
A 3 mg dose of LNG can be considered but women should be informed that the effectiveness of this regimen is unknown.
•A double-dose of UPA-EC is not recommended

▪ Progestogens: EC providers should be aware that the effectiveness of UPA-EC could be reduced.

▪ If a woman takes progestogen in the 5 days after taking UPA-EC, EC providers should be aware that the effectiveness of UPA-EC could theoretically be reduced if a woman has taken progestogen prior to taking UPA-EC.

Contraindications/Restrictions to Use of EC:

•Cu-IUD: EC providers should be aware that the contraindications to insertion of a Cu-IUD for EC are the same as those for routine IUD insertion.
•UPA-EC: EC providers should be aware that UPA-EC is not suitable for use by women who have severe asthma controlled by oral glucocorticoids.

Breastfeeding and Require EC:

•Cu-IUD: Breastfeeding women have a higher relative risk of uterine perforation during insertion of intrauterine contraception than non-breastfeeding women. However, absolute risk of perforation is low.
•UPA-EC: Breastfeeding women should be advised not to breastfeed and to express & discard milk for a week after they have taken UPA-EC.
•LNG-EC: Women who breastfeed should be informed that available limited evidence indicates that LNG-EC has no adverse effects on breastfeeding or on their infants.

Method of EC:

All women requiring EC should be offered a Cu-lUD if appropriate as

it is the most effective method of EC. Cu-IUD can be inserted up to 5 days after the first UPSI in a natural menstrual cycle, or up to 5 days after the earliest likely date of ovulation (whichever is later).

a Cu-IUD is not appropriate or not acceptable; women should be advised that oral EC should be taken as soon as possible if there has been UPSI within the last 5 days

EC providers should consider! UPA-EC as the first-line oral EC for a woman who has had UPSI 96-120 hours ago (even if she has also had UPSI within the last 96 hours).

Sexual assault: Women requiring EC after sexual assault should be offered all methods of EC including the Cu-IUD.

•offer a woman UPA-EC or LNG-EC if she has had UPSI earlier in the same cycle as well as within the last 5 days, as evidence suggests that UPA- EC and LNG-EC do not disrupt an existing pregnancy and are not associated with fetal abnormality.
•If vomiting occurs within 3 hours of taking oral EC, a repeat dose should be given

🔹 Choosing between UPA-EC and LNG-EC

•Ulipristal acetate EC (UPA-EC) has been demonstrated to be more effective than levonorgestrel.
•EC (LNG-EC) from 0–120 hours after UPSI. The evidence suggests that both UPA-EC and LNG-EC are ineffective if taken after ovulation.

METHODS OF EC IN UK

•Women requiring EC who are using enzyme-inducing drugs should be offered a Cu-IUD if appropriate.
•A 3 mg dose of LNG can be considered but women should be informed that the effectiveness of this regimen is unknown. A double-dose of UPA-EC is NOT recommended.

METHODS OF EC IN UK

The effectiveness of UPA-EC could be reduced if a woman takes progestogen in the 5 days after taking UPA-EC.

Effectiveness of UPA-EC could theoretically be reduced if a woman has taken progestogen in the 7 days prior to taking UPA-EC.

Avoid progestogen 7 days before and 5 days after taking UPA-EC.

EMERGENCY CONTRACEPTION

•✅ Adolescents who need EC should be offered all methods of EC including the Cu-IUD.
•✅ Women requiring EC after sexual assault should be offered all methods of EC including the Cu-IUD.

Effectiveness of EC – methods:

•UPA ➜ 98% if taken within 120 hours
•LNG ➜ 85% in 72 hours then decreases to 56% in next 12 hours
•IUCD ➜ 99% effective

IMPORTANT tips before selection of EC

1.after day 19 ➜ use of IUCD if ovulation delayed
2.within day 14 ➜ prefer oral pills
3.LNG – UPSI → 72 hrs. (before midcycle)
4.UPA – UPSI → 120 hrs. (before midcycle <19 days)
5.IUCD – UPSI → 120 hrs. (after midcycle even before midcycle)
6.always keep in mind contra-indications of each EC
